noi_dung:
Penetrate All Dharmas by Reciting Avalokiteshvara

From limitless kalpas in the past until now, we are born only to die, and die only to be born again. Through a span of time stretching hundreds of thousands of myriads of kalpas, we have never once encountered an Avalokiteshvara Dharma assembly. That is why our bad habits and faults have not lessened in the slightest, while our ignorance and afflictions grow greater every day! Now that we have encountered a Dharma assembly of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, we can say it is because the good roots we planted in limitless kalpas past have now ripened that we are able to join such a wonderful and inconceivable Dharma assembly as this. Without good roots, without virtuous conduct, one could never have the chance to join an Avalokiteshvara Session. Therefore, all of you should treasure these seven precious days—do not give rise to discursive thoughts, do not waste time. If you keep indulging in discursive thoughts, then joining this Dharma assembly is as good as not joining, for you will gain no benefit at all!

Although this Dharma assembly only began two days ago, I know that some people have already seen the Bodhisattva, seen light, or seen inconceivable states appear; and some are even about to open the Five Eyes. Therefore, those who have not yet gained any benefit should feel ashamed, and should not assume that because they themselves have gained nothing, others must be the same—that is not so at all!

One could say that Gold Mountain Monastery is a place that "sifts sand in search of gold"—whoever truly wishes to cultivate cannot leave Gold Mountain Monastery, for finding a place to genuinely cultivate is no easy matter. Everyone at Gold Mountain Monastery is a cultivator with resolve for the Way; even in extremely harsh and difficult circumstances, they remain vigorous in applying their skill in cultivation.

There are eighty-four thousand Dharma-doors for cultivating the Way, and you should understand at least a little of each, instead of knowing only one single door. If you have some general idea of every Dharma-door, gradually you will penetrate them all. If you understand only one Dharma-door, it is hard to fathom the "deep as the ocean" state of the Buddhadharma; you would be no different from "a fool peering at the sky through a bamboo tube," convinced that the sky is only as big as the tube's mouth! If you put down the bamboo tube, you will see how vast the sky truly is. Therefore, in studying the Buddhadharma, do not limit yourself to a single Dharma-door—you must penetrate all dharmas and understand all dharmas.

Right now we are reciting the name of Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, and that too is a part of the Buddhadharma. If you have never practiced this Dharma-door, you must come and try it for yourself; do not refuse to cultivate without even trying! If you can complete these full seven days of reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, you will surely reap great benefit for both body and mind. So do not let this opportunity slip by; do not pass up this rare chance before your eyes!

A Bodhisattva cultivates the Six Paramitas and the myriad practices. The Six Paramitas are:

Giving. Giving means we ourselves give to others—not that we want others to give to us.

Patience. Through this Avalokiteshvara Session you will find out

whether or not you have the capacity to endure. One who can endure will surely complete this Avalokiteshvara Session to perfection. One who cannot endure will spend the whole day giving rise to discursive thoughts, such as: "In a little while I'll go to that restaurant and eat my fill," or: "What good does staying here reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name do me? It's useless! I'd better hurry home!"

Without the ability to be patient and to endure, you cannot cultivate the Way! Whether you wish to practice sitting meditation, Buddha-recitation, or reciting Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name—all are fine, for these Dharma-doors are one and the same, with no difference at all. Whichever Dharma-door you cultivate, with patience you will attain accomplishment. Without patience, you cannot cultivate any Dharma-door! A person lacking patience always feels that this is wrong and that is wrong, that nothing is ever right; how could such a person cultivate anything?

The Way fundamentally has no view of self, no attachment to "I"; therefore, whoever clings to self can never cultivate the Way! Someone says: "I want to investigate Chan!" You want to investigate Chan? Then you need patience all the more!

Moral discipline. To uphold the precepts is: "Commit no evil, practice all good."

Vigor. Vigor means diligence, not laziness or laxity.

Samadhi. Right now we recite Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva's name, praying that Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva will help us attain samadhi.

Wisdom. Once samadhi is attained, wisdom arises. Thus these six practices are all interrelated.

Someone says: "I like to specialize in samadhi." Then let me now tell you how to cultivate samadhi. Once you have stepped into the Chan Hall, no matter what happens, you may not leave the Chan Hall even half a step! Someone asks: "What if I get sick?" If you're sick, then just be sick! Sick or not, you still investigate Chan as usual!

"But what if I die?" Even dead, your corpse may not be carried out of the Chan Hall! If a meditator dies, the body is tucked beneath an empty sitting bench, and even if it putrefies it must stay there—it may not be taken outside. The dead may not leave the Chan Hall either!

Someone says: "Isn't that just like being in prison?" Do you think you aren't in prison right now? Everyone is locked inside a prison of their own, only they do not realize it! Your own nature wants to get out but cannot get out; wants to return but cannot return. Once out, you cannot come back; once back, you cannot get out again—can that be called "freedom"? Each person's body is itself a prison; only, you have not yet understood this!

During a Chan Session, once you have entered the Chan Hall you may not step out of its doors again. Whoever goes out gets a beating—the fragrant board whistling down on head and back. That is during a Chan Session. It is the same during an Avalokiteshvara Session—no one may leave the Buddha Hall! Whoever disobeys will be beaten, for—who told you to come here in the first place!?

Someone says: "I came because I read the announcement." But the announcement never said that once here you could leave as you please! If you want to go, fine—but first you must pay for everyone's meals before you may leave; otherwise, you cannot go. Why? Because if you leave, others will see you and follow your example. You leave, she leaves, he leaves too, and soon everyone has left—that is "destroying the Way-place." So to avoid the offense of "destroying the Way-place," you must pay for everyone's food. If you cannot afford it, best not to leave!

You all have good affinities with one another, which is why you have come together to Gold Mountain Monastery. Without good affinities, there would be no way you could even set foot past Gold Mountain Monastery's threshold. Having good affinities, do not hesitate to befriend one another in this Avalokiteshvara Dharma assembly. Support one another and advance forward together. Forward to where? To wherever the depths of your hearts wish to go. Each of us should help others. Why do I say this? Because I fear you may take a wrong turn and get lost!

(Avalokiteshvara Session, March 15, 1976)
